guides.contentMarkdown:
# DSWD crisis assistance (AICS)

The **Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations** program supports people and families facing a crisis. DSWD's 2025 charter covers indigent, marginalized, vulnerable, disadvantaged, and financially incapacitated applicants, subject to a social worker's assessment. Assistance can include medical, funeral, food, transportation, psychosocial support, and referrals. [1]

## Prepare your documents

Bring your **original valid government-issued ID and two photocopies**, as specified in the 2025 charter. Examples include National ID, UMID, SSS/GSIS, PhilHealth, PRC, and OWWA/OFW ID. [1]

Prepare the records relevant to your request. DSWD's AICS FAQ lists these examples; documents are submitted as originals or certified true copies. [2]

| Request | Supporting records |
| --- | --- |
| Hospital bill | Medical certificate, clinical abstract, discharge summary, or other accepted medical record; hospital bill or statement of account. For an outstanding obligation, certificate of balance or promissory note. |
| Medicines | Medical record and prescription or treatment protocol; price quotation as applicable. |
| Laboratory examination | Doctor's order or laboratory request and official price quotation. |
| Funeral expenses | Death certificate or accepted death certification; funeral contract or statement of account. Outstanding obligations may require a balance certificate or promissory note. |
| Transportation | Documents establishing the circumstance, such as a medical certificate, death certificate, police certification, court order, or subpoena, depending on the request. |

## Application process

1. Present the documents for screening through DSWD's crisis-intervention service. The charter identifies CIS, SWAD, satellite offices, and Malasakit Centers as delivery channels. [1]
2. Attend the social worker's interview and assessment. The worker evaluates the actual need, documentary evidence, eligibility, appropriate service, and any financial assistance recommended for approval. [3]
3. After approval, follow the release instructions for the assistance or referral. [3]

**Assistance is assessed individually.** The amount depends on actual need, supporting records, and program funds; an application does not establish a fixed entitlement. [3]

## Sources

1. [DSWD — 2025 Unified Citizen's Charter, 2nd edition, onsite AICS service](https://fo6.dswd.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/2025-2nd-Edition-DSWD-Unified-Citizens-Charter.pdf)
2. [DSWD — AICS/AKAP frequently asked questions, AICS documentary requirements](https://aics.dswd.gov.ph/about-us/faqs/)
3. [DSWD — Memorandum Circular 15, series of 2022, individual-client screening, assessment, and release](https://aics.dswd.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/MC_2022-015.pdf)

National program information for residents of Siquijor. Source review: **17 November 2026**.

guides.contentMarkdown:
# First-time adult Philippine passport

Apply for your first Philippine passport as an adult. Prepare your documents, book an appointment, and check the application fees below.

## Bring to your appointment

- Confirmed online appointment, completed application form, and DFA payment e-receipt.
- Documentary proof of Philippine citizenship. For a natural-born applicant, this includes a PSA-issued Certificate of Live Birth or Report of Birth. The charter also identifies separate citizenship records for foundlings, naturalized citizens, and people who elected, retained, or reacquired Philippine citizenship.
- At least one accepted valid ID, such as PhilID/ePhilID or another government ID accepted by DFA.
- For women choosing their spouse's surname: PSA-issued Certificate of Marriage or Report of Marriage.

**Bring the original documents and ID, with one photocopy for submission. Personal appearance is required.** Supporting records depend on citizenship and personal circumstances. [1]

## Published domestic fees

DFA's **2025 charter** publishes these charges. [1]

| Charge | Philippine pesos |
| --- | ---: |
| Regular passport application | ₱950 |
| Expedited passport application | ₱1,200 |
| Additional convenience fee | ₱50 |

## Application stages

1. Book through the official passport appointment system and complete the payment step.
2. Attend your selected consular office. Present your printed application and ID for appointment verification.
3. Submit the required records for document evaluation.
4. Complete passport enrollment: information encoding, document scanning, photograph, and biometrics.
5. Follow the release instructions and check the passport's details when you receive it. [2]

DFA states that **appointment booking is free**. The application fees above are separate from obtaining an appointment. [3]

[Book a DFA passport appointment](https://passport.gov.ph/appointment/)

## Sources

1. [DFA — 2025 Citizen's Charter, first edition: adult requirements and domestic passport fee table](https://dfa.gov.ph/images/2025/transparency/DFA_Citizens_Charter_2025_1st_Edition_1.pdf)
2. [DFA — 2024 Citizen's Charter, first edition, domestic passport application workflow](https://dfa.gov.ph/images/2024/transparency/DFA_Citizens_Charter_2024_1st_Edition.pdf)
3. [DFA — Official passport appointment system](https://passport.gov.ph/appointment/)
